papers.title: Automated Sleep Staging Performance Across Two Experimental Sleep Manipulation Protocols in Adolescents.
papers.summary: Evaluated POPS, YASA, and combined POPS+YASA automated sleep staging against manual polysomnography in adolescents across a sleep restriction protocol (N=43) and a slow-wave sleep deprivation protocol (N=18). Agreement was moderate-to-substantial (Cohen's k 0.53–0.76) but declined under sleep restriction (poorer Wake/N1/N2 classification) and on the SWSD night (poorer N3 classification), indicating performance is less consistent when sleep is curtailed or fragmented.

papers.title: Cross-Band Coupling of EEG Infraslow Oscillations during NREM Sleep in Mice.
papers.summary: Analyzed cross-band coupling of EEG infraslow oscillations (0.01-0.03 Hz) across six frequency bands during NREM sleep in mice, finding that alpha, sigma, beta, and theta ISOs form a strongly correlated and phase-locked motif replicated in wild-type and LepR-Cre transgenic mice, while gamma coupling was moderate and delta was uncorrelated or absent.

papers.title: High-fat diet-induced MAFLD is associated with sleep architecture disruption via hippocampal neuroinflammation and bifurcated IRS-1/Akt/mTOR signaling in mice.
papers.summary: Fed male BALB/c mice a 60% high-fat diet for 16 weeks to model MAFLD and assessed 24-h EEG/EMG sleep along with hippocampal neuroinflammation and IRS-1/Akt/mTOR signaling. HFD mice showed reduced NREM and REM sleep, fragmentation, reduced NREM delta power, dampened circadian delta rhythm, hippocampal neuronal injury and elevated TNF-α/IL-1β, with increased p-IRS-1 (Ser307), decreased p-Akt (Ser473), and elevated p-mTOR (Ser2448).

papers.title: CADENCE: Open-source software for signal conditioning, feature extraction, visualization and analysis of cardiac optical mapping data.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Developed CADENCE, an open-source MATLAB-based pipeline for cardiac optical mapping that combines signal conditioning, feature extraction, and analysis in an end-to-end application. CADENCE was validated across four species and multiple tissue and camera configurations, showing agreement with blinded experts comparable to inter-observer variability and median dominant frequency error of 0.03%.

papers.title: Characterising sleep spindle emergence in infancy: Effects of prematurity and early locomotor intervention
papers.summary: Characterized sleep spindle temporal and spatial organization using daytime high-density EEG in 50 infants (12 full-term, 38 very preterm, 12 of whom received locomotor training) at 2 months corrected age. Rhythmic spindle organization was present in all groups at about one-third adult rate and was unaffected by prematurity or training, while untrained preterm infants showed more diffuse spindle-band activity and trained preterm infants showed a full-term-like spatial distribution with lower frontal spindle density.

papers.title: REM sleep infraslow rhythms correlate with neuropsychiatric symptom severity.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional polysomnographic study of 59 male veterans, REM infraslow respiratory rate oscillations were higher in frequency in those with more severe neuropsychiatric symptoms, while conventional REM metrics showed no significant correlations. Eye movements occurred preferentially during specific phases of infraslow oscillations, suggesting a potential physiological biomarker.

papers.title: Beyond reduced alpha power: a weaker temporal link between alpha and other brain rhythms in Alzheimer's disease
papers.summary: Analyzed eyes-closed resting EEG from 29 healthy controls, 36 AD patients, and 23 FTD patients using a vector autoregressive model to quantify alpha's predictive contribution (G) to later theta, beta, and gamma activity. G was lower in AD than controls (adjusted difference -3.19×10^3, 95% CI -5.25 to -1.13, p=0.0035), retained 75.8% of the difference after adjusting for alpha power and signal quality, and added information beyond alpha expression, suggesting a weaker temporal link between alpha and other rhythms in AD.

papers.title: Whole-brain normative modeling across multiple functional connectivity metrics in MEG
papers.summary: Proposed M/EEG-FUNCOIN, a normative modeling framework that captures age- and sex-related whole-brain functional connectivity dimensions from multiple MEG metrics (amplitude envelope correlation, phase-locking value, time-delay embedding covariance). Applied to Cam-CAN resting-state MEG, it characterized connectivity patterns in greater detail than existing methods and captured meaningful connectivity deviations in individuals ranking high and low in cognitive ability.

papers.title: Longitudinal Imaging in a Mouse Model of Focal Cortical Dysplasia Reveals Lesion Expansion and Loss of Pre-Discharge Neuronal Recruitment
papers.summary: Combined chronic two-photon calcium imaging through a cranial window with video-EEG in an in utero electroporation mouse model of focal cortical dysplasia type II carrying the mTOR p.L2427P variant. The lesion progressively expanded in adulthood (partly via dysmorphic neuron somatic growth), and in seizing mice dysmorphic and pyramidal neuron activity declined while reliable pre-interictal-discharge neuronal recruitment present in non-seizing cortex was lost at late stages.

papers.title: Lifespan Trajectories of Resting State Bipolar EEG Power.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Derived lifespan trajectories of resting-state bipolar EEG power from 12,906 observations in 5,781 participants aged 12-70 without alcohol use disorder, analyzing seven frequency bands and 24 bipolar channels. EEG power decreased sharply from age 12 to the early 20s, followed by divergent patterns including increases in beta frequencies and mixed theta/alpha changes, with striking sex differences in inter-frequency correlation trajectories.

papers.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials Across Cognitive States: Awake, Sleep, Sedation, and Anesthesia.
papers.summary: This review presents a state-aware framework for interpreting auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) across wakefulness, natural sleep, pharmacologic sedation, general anesthesia, and impaired consciousness, linking latency ranges to ascending generators and later cortical context dependence. It concludes that an AEP is interpretable only when generator, stimulus, analysis domain, recording conditions, and cognitive state are considered together.

papers.title: A Bayesian functional model with multilevel partition priors for group studies in neuroscience.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a Bayesian model-based clustering approach for functional data using a multilevel partition prior to simultaneously assess group effects and individual deviations in neuroscientific recordings. Simulation studies showed correct classification under varying noise levels, and an EEG case study provided new insights into brain mechanisms during object recognition.

papers.title: Phase-dependent EEG decoding of continuous visual stimuli.
papers.summary: Recorded EEG while participants viewed 2-s Gabor patches and applied phase-dependent decoding to test whether alpha phase modulates visual representation strength. Decoding accuracy varied systematically with alpha phase in a unimodal profile peaking over occipito-parietal electrodes, indicating more accurate visual representation at specific alpha phases during continuous input.

papers.title: A Complementary Dual-Branch Receptive Field Network for Cross-Channel-Density Motor Imagery EEG Decoding.
papers.summary: A complementary dual-branch receptive field network (DBRFNet) was proposed for cross-channel-density motor imagery EEG decoding, capturing multi-scale temporal dynamics through two branches with progressive spatio-temporal modules. DBRFNet achieved decoding accuracies of 80.48%, 84.37%, and 92.24% under cross-validation on three public datasets, demonstrating competitive performance.

papers.title: Transcranial Evoked Potentials are Minimally Influenced by Afferent Feedback From Peripheral Muscle Contraction.
papers.summary: Combined M1 TMS-EEG with electromyography, accelerometry, and peripheral electrical stimulation to dissociate central from peripheral contributions to TMS-evoked potentials. Larger motor outputs covaried with distinct EEG morphologies across all time windows including pre-feedback latencies, whereas isolated muscle contraction produced only delayed (>65 ms) small responses, indicating TMS-evoked potentials mainly reflect baseline motor cortex excitability.

papers.title: A Modality-Invariant Measure of Neural Health.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The Neural Health Index (NHI), a single physiological marker based on spatial distribution of signal-derived energy correlates in the resting brain, was developed and validated across 808 participants. NHI distinguished healthy from clinical populations with >95% sensitivity and specificity, scaled with disease severity, and generalized across diagnoses and modalities.

papers.title: Neurophysiological and Psychophysical Biomarkers for Predicting Spinal Cord Stimulation Treatment Response in Chronic Neuropathic Pain: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 12 studies on neurophysiological and psychophysical biomarkers for predicting spinal cord stimulation response in chronic neuropathic pain, finding the strongest signal in preoperative somatosensory evoked potentials and resting EEG/MEG spectral features. All included studies were at high risk of bias, and the two prediction models (76–88% internal accuracy, AUC up to 0.88) lacked external validation.

papers.title: Spatial Neurophysiological Gradients at High Resolution Differentiate Tumor Types in the Human Cortex at the Tumor-Brain Interface.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Intraoperative EEG recordings from 100 participants revealed that spatially resolved aperiodic exponent and high-gamma activity gradients differentiate IDH-mutant glioma, IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, and metastases, with beta coherence reduced in IDH-mutant tumors. Physiological abnormalities extended into radiographically normal-appearing brain, indicating tumor-type-dependent signatures.

papers.title: A Novel Digital Phenotype of Physical Activity: Associations with Heart Rate Fragmentation.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 602 older male veterans, Gaussian mixture modeling of accelerometry across six physical activity domains identified two overlapping phenotypes (compact-early and diffuse-late). The diffuse-late phenotype was associated with higher heart rate fragmentation (PIP and IALS), linking activity timing and dispersion to neuroautonomic dysregulation.

papers.title: Physiological Signals Boosted by Artificial Intelligence Save Time and Brain Function.
papers.summary: This review examines AI and machine learning applications in neurocritical care, using continuous EEG, intracranial pressure, and cerebral blood flow data to detect subclinical deterioration. Through three illustrative cases it explores AI use for delayed cerebral ischemia, real-time seizure detection, and physiological nowcasting, while noting current tools remain largely in developmental or validation stages.

papers.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Designed and tested three 3D-printed, hair-anchored EEG electrode attachments for Type 4a–4c Afro-textured hairstyles in 17 adults, comparing them with a conventional 16-electrode cap. The novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance, cut electrode disconnection from 20% to 0.1%, and improved signal quality (alpha power and 1/f component) without changing comfort.

papers.title: Covert attentional tracking with invisible phase tagging
papers.summary: This RIFT-EEG experiment (n=24) used phase modulation to create 8 unique invisible tags, showing that visual processing can be measured at multiple locations tagged with identical frequency but different phases. Combining phase- and frequency-modulated tagging allowed quantification of the distribution of covert attention across the visual field.

papers.title: Brief Trains of Closed-loop TMS Induce Controllable Power in FM-theta Oscillations.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Tested whether brief trains of 6 Hz TMS locked to real-time frontal-midline theta phase modulate post-train theta power in six healthy adults during a working memory task. Trough-triggered trains transiently increased total and induced FM-theta power compared to peak-triggered trains, with a robust subject-level effect (Cohen's dz = 1.32) and no evoked effect.

papers.title: Vibrotactile transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) during working memory: convergent electrophysiological evidence for cortical efficiency.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Tested sensory-amplification versus cortical-efficiency hypotheses for vibrotactile taVNS during N-back working memory in 20 healthy adults (EEG, ECG, eye-tracking) and 19 epilepsy patients with intracranial monitoring. Active vtaVNS reduced scalp visual ERPs and temporal high-gamma responses versus sham, smaller visual ERPs were linked to successful 4-back encoding, and vtaVNS shifted cortical dynamics toward criticality, supporting enhanced cortical efficiency.

papers.title: Treadmill or Overground? Cognitive-Motor Interference Effects in Healthy Older Individuals.
papers.summary: Compared cognitive-motor interference during outdoor overground walking versus indoor treadmill walking in 36 healthy older adults using an auditory Go/No-Go dual-task paradigm with mobile EEG and motion tracking. Dual-task interference was significant in both walking conditions but more pronounced during overground walking, suggesting greater competition for shared cognitive resources in naturalistic locomotion.

papers.title: When the heart and the brain meet: Brain-heart interactions in feature integration
papers.summary: Reanalyzed a dataset of 25 participants to examine heartbeat-locked neural activity during a visual feature integration task requiring shape-color binding while inhibiting distractors. Prestimulus heart-evoked potential amplitude briefly differed between correct and incorrect integrations, and heart-evoked oscillations showed alpha and low beta modulations before target onset that depended on cardiac timing.

papers.title: High-dose cerium dioxide nanorods induce behavioral and electroencephalographic abnormalities through 5-HT1B receptor signaling disruption with an evaluation of anpirtoline's therapeutic potential.
papers.summary: Investigated neurotoxicity of high-dose cerium dioxide nanorods in vitro and after intranasal instillation in mice, finding neuronal apoptosis, hippocampal and striatal accumulation, abnormal exploratory behaviors, heightened seizure susceptibility, and altered EEG oscillations. Multi-omic profiling indicated disrupted serotonin metabolism via 5-HT1B receptor downregulation, and pharmacological activation of 5-HT1B with anpirtoline partially reversed the behavioral and EEG abnormalities.

papers.title: Clinical feature-guided targeted genetic testing in early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy: a real-world diagnostic approach in a resource-limited setting.
papers.summary: Prospectively evaluated clinical feature-guided targeted sequencing of 108 DEE-associated genes in 51 Vietnamese children with early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were found in 49% overall, with higher diagnostic yield in the hypothesis-driven group (93.3% vs 30.6%), and 20 of 25 genetically diagnosed patients had treatment changes accompanied by at least 50% seizure reduction.

papers.title: Axonal dysfunction precedes axonal degeneration in a mouse model of progressive parkinsonism.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Comparing dopaminergic axons in the MitoPark mouse model of Parkinsonism with age-matched controls, this study found reduced action potential-evoked calcium signals and impaired action potential propagation with altered axonal waveforms well before dopaminergic fiber loss and motor deficits. These findings define an early period of axon-specific physiological dysfunction preceding axonal degeneration.

papers.title: Internet Intervention for Functional Seizures: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In this 3-arm randomized clinical trial of 107 adults with functional seizures, a self-guided internet-based intervention plus standard care produced greater reductions in monthly seizure frequency than standard care (RR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.18–0.69) sustained through 12 months, with improvements in anxiety and depression. The therapist-guided arm improved anxiety at 6 months but did not significantly reduce seizure frequency, and no adverse events occurred.

papers.title: Conductive Polyvinyl Alcohol-Based Hydrogels for Wearable Electronics: Preparation Strategies, Conductivity Enhancement, and Sensing Applications.
papers.summary: This review surveys fabrication strategies, conductivity-enhancement routes (electronic, ionic, and hybrid), and wearable sensing applications of conductive PVA-based hydrogels, citing representative values such as tensile strengths above 19 MPa, conductivities above 10 S/m, gauge factors above 10, and self-healing within 1 s. It emphasizes gaps in reproducibility, comparable testing protocols, device-level integration, and scalability for clinical translation.

papers.title: Sedation Versus General Anesthesia During Pediatric Electrophysiology Studies: A Paired Comparison.
papers.summary: In a prospective paired comparison of 51 pediatric patients with supraventricular tachycardia studied under both procedural sedation and general anesthesia in the same session, overall tachycardia inducibility was higher under sedation (78.4%) than general anesthesia (56.9%, p = 0.007). Accessory pathway effective refractory period was prolonged under general anesthesia, while other electrophysiological parameters did not differ significantly.

papers.title: Gamma-ray spectrum unfolding and air-absorbed dose-rate estimation using a two-stage spectral learning framework.
papers.summary: Developed a two-stage spectral learning framework that first unfolds gamma-ray spectra using a LaBr3:Ce response matrix (591 Geant4 monoenergetic spectra, 4000 mixed spectra) and then regresses air-absorbed dose rate. The unfolding model reached R² 0.932 and the tri-branch dose-regression model reached R² 0.993 with MAPE 1.78%, and application to a measured soil spectrum supported the sequential detector-to-dose workflow.

papers.title: The Architecture of Selectivity: Molecular Basis of BlTx2 Discrimination Among Kv Channels and Kv4 Isoforms.
papers.summary: Mapped the molecular determinants of Kv4.1-selective inhibition by the α-KTx15 scorpion toxin BlTx2 using electrophysiology, mutagenesis, tandem chimeras, structural modeling, and evolutionary analysis. Canonical pore-blocking residues Lys27/Tyr36 were essential, Kv4.1 Asn355 was identified as a key barrier to toxin activity, and pore-facing versus peripheral toxin residues were shown to underlie conserved inhibition and potency tuning, respectively.

papers.title: Toward Reliable Patient-Specific Aortic Strain Mapping from 4D CTA: Validation, Spectral Structure, and Clinical Potential.
papers.summary: This preprint develops and validates a framework for spatially resolved ascending aortic strain mapping from 4D CTA using nnU-Net segmentation, remeshing, deformable registration, and mesh-based strain estimation, with low bias relative to finite-element reference strains. Laplace-Beltrami spectral reconstruction reduced segmentation-related disagreement by 52-56%, and 95th-percentile areal strain was inversely associated with aortic diameter, aortic height index, and age.

papers.title: Lead Exposure During Differentiation Perturbs Electrophysiological Function in iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes in a Cell Line-Dependent Manner.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint exposed two human iPSC lines to lead (0.5 or 5 µM) during the first 8 days of ventricular cardiomyocyte differentiation and found persistent, concentration- and cell line-dependent changes in calcium transients and action potential dynamics, including increased arrhythmias in both lines. Calcium transporter/channel and potassium channel gene expression was unchanged, suggesting post-translational mechanisms.

papers.title: An AI-Enabled Translational Drug Discovery Framework for NALCN Channelopathy: From High-Throughput Screening to Therapeutic Candidate.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports an AI-enabled drug-repurposing framework integrating phenotypic high-throughput screening of ~1,200 approved drugs, Boltz-2 structural modeling, and experimental validation to identify NALCN inhibitors for CLIFAHDD. Aprepitant emerged as the lead candidate, partially inhibiting NALCN sodium leak currents (IC50 2.22 µM) and rescuing hyperlocomotor and dystonic phenotypes in a C. elegans gain-of-function model.

papers.title: Antibody-Related Mechanisms in Ocular Diseases: Autoimmunity, Malignancy, and Therapeutic Targeting.
papers.summary: Narrative review integrating antibody and B-cell biology across autoimmune, paraneoplastic, and malignant ocular diseases, distinguishing direct antibody pathogenicity from disease association and proposing a mechanistically stratified framework for diagnosis and targeted therapy.

papers.title: 14-3-3 Enables β-Adrenergic Regulation of the Cardiac Sodium Channel at the Intercalated Disc
papers.summary: Using patch-clamp, proximity ligation, mutagenesis, and CRISPR-engineered iPSC-CMs, this study shows that 14-3-3 and Nav1.5 residue S460 mediate β-adrenergic enhancement of sodium current specifically at the intercalated disc, supporting increased cardiac conduction velocity.

papers.title: Activation pathway of the human voltage-gated proton channel.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Integrating constant-pH molecular dynamics, weighted-ensemble path sampling, and AlphaFold modeling with electrophysiology and smFRET, this study resolves the activation pathway of human voltage-gated proton channel hHV1, revealing voltage-driven S4 displacement with countercharge reorganization and lipid-dependent stabilization of the activated state.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
